ground_truth.description: The new __init__.py guidance states as a blanket rule that for cross_project findings 'cite_task is the sole dedup anchor there', but the stage2.py section it cross-references defines two sub-cases: only sub-case (1) (a local task is the subject) has a cite_task anchor; in sub-case (2) (work lives entirely in the unknown target project) cite_task returns unknown_project and attaches nothing, so the finding is deduped by its normalised description — not by cite_task. The summary overgeneralizes and can mislead the recon agent for the target-project-only case.

task.title: Fix stage2.py STAGE2_SYSTEM_PROMPT cross_project section to instruct cite_task for cross_project findings
task.description: The cross_project section of STAGE2_SYSTEM_PROMPT (~L100-106 in stage2.py) does not instruct Stage 2 to call cite_task when emitting cross_project findings. This means cross_project findings have empty cited_tasks → _derive_affected_ids returns [] → compute_content_fingerprint hashes only the drifting description text → the finding re-escalates every reconciliation cycle without being folded by the cross-cycle dedup machinery. The fix (task 1573) landed compute_flag_signature falling back to cited_tasks[0].task_id, but only works when Stage 2 actually attaches citations. Without the prompt instruction, Stage 2 never does.
task.details: Fix: update the STAGE2_SYSTEM_PROMPT Cross-Project Routing section to include an explicit instruction like: 'When emitting a cross_project finding, always call cite_task(finding_id, project_id, task_id) for the local task whose scope has been rerouted, even when that task_id is the source task being re-scoped or cancelled. This provides the task_id anchor that compute_content_fingerprint needs to fold duplicate findings cross-cycle.' Also verify the instruction is present in the actual cross_project routing guidance paragraph so future Stage 2 runs inherit it. See memory cfe9adc3 for the gap analysis.
